summary: Round-2 verify, docs only, no test bytes staged; scope was my two round-1 majors and anything the fixes introduced. BOTH FIXED, and both verified against the artifacts rather than against the prose. TR-M0.75-1: the clause is now 'THE DIRECTION IS NOT SAFE' and every load-bearing part of it checks out in the tree. The measurement window IS a Thread.sleep -- LocalSequencerRenewTest.java:415 `Thread.sleep(1000)` between two `store.counts().puts()` reads (:410, :416), with the comment at :412-414 saying so itself -- so an overrun lowers the count through the renewer's 150ms sleeps and raises it through the window, and the row's 'fixes neither the sign nor the size' is right. The recorded series is verbatim from TR-M4.17-3 (.harness/review/e8a3151c...test-reviewer.json): '6 (three idle runs), 6 (two runs under 32 spinners on 20 cores), 7 (two runs at load average 123)' -- the loaded sample IS the maximum. The committed slack is at LocalSequencerRenewTest.java:389-390, 'Honest is 6-7 even at load average 124, so a floor of 4 keeps ~1.75x slack': 7/4 = 1.75, the idle sample gives 6/4 = 1.5, so 'quotes the loaded value' is accurate, and the grep-evasion claim holds for that site because 'load' and 'average' wrap across :389/:390. The mutant-survival half is arithmetically right and is the case the retracted premise could not cover: bound `isBetween(4L, 30L)` (:422), 1000ms window, 150ms interval, 2x = 300ms, 1000/300 = 3.33, inclusive floor 4 reachable by one added tick. AND IT DOES NOT OVERCLAIM IN EITHER DIRECTION: it states explicitly that it does NOT claim the 4s were artifacts, gives phase alone as about one in three (P(4 ticks) at 3.33 expected with uniform phase = 1/3, consistent with M4.41's measured 'killed 2 of 5'), and lands on the question being OPEN. That is my finding stated correctly, no wider. TR-M0.75-2: 'load average ~206' is verbatim in a PRODUCTION verdict -- .harness/review/68c714405ad5...reviewer.json, role reviewer, task M4.43, finding M4.43-R1d: 'I measured the same configuration in my own tree ... load average ~206) and got fast=6, fast=7, fast=7'. Those three runs are one of the two samples behind M4.41's floor of 9 (backlog-notes.md:309: 'fastRate=7 slowRate=1 (3 of 3) in one tree and fastRate=6,7,7 in another ... A floor of 9 clears both modes'), so 'ALSO a reviewer's recorded figure' and the M4.41 linkage are both true, and the 'earlier draft reattributed it to this session's own uptime' self-correction is accurate. NOTHING NEW INTRODUCED that I could refute: M4.45's quotation is verbatim across FakeSequencerTest.java:208-210 including the trailing clause, its reciprocal reading is right (surviving 1 in 6 means failing about 5 in 6), and 6! = 720 checks. ON THE TWO PRODUCTION MINORS THE AUTHOR IS RECORDING: I CONCUR THAT NEITHER BLOCKS, and I checked both independently rather than taking them on report. (1) `grep -n 'load average' baselines/review.txt` returns exactly one hit, line 18, which is `rounds:M4.43`; `rounds:M4.17` is line 17 and carries no such figure. So the row is one line off AND the 'both evade the obvious grep' half is false of that site -- the sharper form of the minor, worth having in the commit body alongside the ID, since a fix session greps the ID the row names, finds nothing, and can conclude the row is wrong while the real site sits one line below. It costs a round, not the evidence. (2) 17e54d6's body does carry the refuted reasoning verbatim -- 'Sleeps overrun rather than undershoot, so honest-rate floors measured under it are conservative' -- so 'an earlier draft of this row' understates where it lives; a commit body cannot be edited, the corrective content IS in the artifact a session picking M0.75 loads, and the remedy is one clause. Both are minor. I did NOT hunt further: the backlog.md headline mentions only 123 and 186 as reviewer figures, which is true as written with the ~206 correction carried in the note a picker reads, so I am not filing it.
